value.rationale: The object is an exceptional edge-transitive but nonvertex-transitive canonical golden-rhombus zonohedron. The problem asks for the intrinsic largest tetrahedron and the full equality locus, natural finite-volume invariants. The answer is unexpectedly mixed between the two vertex orbits: all 20 maxima use three icosahedron points and one dodecahedron point, while the famous ten regular inscribed tetrahedra are suboptimal. The exact sharp ratio and rigid classification serve as reference benchmarks for extremal inscribed-simplex geometry; no universal theorem is claimed.
